paper.title_en: Hybrid Simulations of Proton Acceleration at Oblique High-$β$ Shocks
paper.abstract_en: Collisionless shocks in the intracluster and intergalactic medium (ICM/IGM) are expected to energize both electrons and ions. While electron acceleration is revealed by prominent radio emission, $γ$-ray emission from hadronic interactions remains undetected, suggesting that high-$β$ (ratio of thermal to magnetic pressure), low-Mach-number shocks cannot accelerate protons efficiently. We present three-dimensional hybrid simulations of quasi-perpendicular shocks with sonic Mach numbers $M_s\sim{3.4{-}17.5}$, focusing primarily on high-$β$ conditions representative of cluster environments and including several lower-$β$ comparison runs. We find that weak shocks with $M_s\lesssim5$ are consistently inefficient, with $\varepsilon_{\rm CR}\lesssim0.1\%$, while inefficient cases can persist to substantially higher $M_s$ depending on $M_A$ and $β$. In contrast, stronger shocks ($M_s \gtrsim 10$) develop clear power-law tails with slopes $q \sim 4.0$ and reach $\varepsilon_{\rm CR} \sim 3\%$. These results suggest that weak, oblique ICM shocks are generally unlikely to accelerate protons efficiently. However, reducing $\vartheta_{B_n}$ to $\sim 45^\circ$ leads to substantially higher acceleration efficiencies, indicating that magnetic obliquity plays a critical role in determining proton acceleration. Our findings provide a microphysical framework for interpreting radio relic observations, whose polarization suggests that electrons are accelerated at oblique shocks, and the absence of cluster $γ$-ray detections.
